routing_case.scenario: Coordinator has an image-generation skill; child has an image tool but no generation skill and no vision; separate reviewer can see images.

coordinator.roles: Owns scope, decisions, dispatch, and final evidence. Because it holds the image-generation skill (and assuming its skill-specified execution path is usable), it is the qualified generation owner: it may ask the user about generation and/or generate, or relay its own concrete generation question through the child. It may also relay. It must attribute visual findings to the qualified reviewer rather than claim to have seen images itself (coordinator may be text-only).
coordinator.condition: Only with the generation skill available to it AND a usable generation path per that skill's instructions; skill identity and path must be recorded.

child.roles: Structural/code worker and/or Unity operator / capture worker only (if its project access is separately verified). The standalone image tool does not qualify it: per image-asset-workflow.md a standalone tool, API, or credentials do not satisfy the generation-skill prerequisite. Without vision it cannot do raster analysis, visual asset matching, crop bounds, or screenshot fidelity claims; as a visionless operator it returns technical evidence and images for review, not a visual PASS.
child.reason: The generation question and generation must both belong to a verified skill-owning executor; the child has neither the skill nor vision. Coordinator relaying the question does not transfer qualification, and skill-on-A + tool-on-B does not qualify either automatically.

reviewer.roles: Visual analyst / asset reviewer and Visual QA reviewer, provided its vision is verified for the exact actual images (mockup and generated candidates) at required sizes. Vision does not grant user art acceptance; candidate proposals still need the existing review decision.
